approach: Root cause: an executable is written and run in the same process while a write handle (or a forked child that copied it) still holds the file. Four earlier jobs guarded only the last symptom. Every test stand-in already goes through athena_testkit::write_executable except the `script` helper in the slot_exec.rs unit tests, so the fix has four parts. (1) Widen the scan in no_in_process_exec_writes.rs. A wrapper is a fn (header `fn name(` or `fn name<`) whose brace-counted body holds a raw permission call AND sets an execute bit (an octal literal with an odd digit not preceded by `!`, a `+x` string, or a chmod-argument line). Calls to wrappers are flagged: same-file wrappers always, pub/pub(crate) wrappers in other files of the same crate. A chmod-in-argument rule covers `sh -c`, .arg/.args and split Command::new. The span of a write_executable( call is skipped, ending at the first line where paren depth returns to zero, counted outside plain, raw and char literals; a call that never closes within 40 lines is not skipped past its first line (fails closed). Fixtures fail on each bad shape and pass on the helper. (2) Convert the slot_exec.rs `script` helper and drop its EXEMPT entry. (3) Move the ETXTBSY retry out of claude.rs into athena_agent::procs (pub retry_busy and retry_busy_with, 20 x 50 ms, libc::ETXTBSY only) and use it at each production site whose tests feed it a stand-in; xtask gets a private std-only copy. (4) Record it: CHANGELOG Fixed entry whose first sentence is the root cause, D163 with the site table, a D160->D163 link. Round 3 answers: findings 1-5 (files outside the reading's deliverables) are kept on purpose and justified in decision 1, with the user question left open; finding 6 (the wrapper rule flagged any mode setter, e.g. claude.rs write_private with mode 0o600) is fixed by requiring an execute-bit signal and dropping the fragile write-bit exclusion; finding 7 (bare-name cross-file matching, generic headers, char-literal braces) by same-crate matching, `fn name<` headers and literal-aware scanning; finding 8 (raw strings stretching the skip) by literal-aware depth counting that ends at the first zero; finding 9 by naming the new tests with `busy` and stating the count. The scan is a test lint, not an athena-core admission or reading-check rule, so crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs is not touched and no corpus case applies; the input forms are mapped to fixtures instead.

Sites: checks.rs run_check spawn (~456), reading.rs BinaryChecker::check (~4679), gh/transport.rs GhCli::gh (~23), run/mod.rs run_bounded (~366), slot_exec.rs real-cargo status (~92), claude.rs (89, 340); xtask `found` and `check_credentials` use a private copy.

Each edit is one line around an existing spawn/output/status call, with messages unchanged. athena-core and athena-cli already list athena-agent in [dependencies] (core Cargo.toml:12, cli Cargo.toml:16), so no Cargo.toml edit and no new file are needed. The findings are minor scope notes, not a defect; the user question below lets the user narrow it.

decisions.choice: Wrapper detection (answers finding 6 and 7). A fn is a wrapper when its brace-counted body contains BOTH a raw permission call (`set_permissions(`, `from_mode(`, `.set_mode(`, or `.mode(` with an argument) AND an execute-bit signal: an octal literal `0o[0-7]+` with at least one odd digit that is not directly preceded by `!`, or the text `+x` inside a string, or a chmod-argument line. The write-bit exclusion from round 2 is dropped as unnecessary: the write-bit toggles in pin.rs:186-191, core/snapshot.rs:188-192 and git/snapshot.rs:440-445 use only `| 0o200` and `& !0o222`, which have no odd digit. Header match covers `fn name(` and `fn name<` after optional pub, pub(crate), const, unsafe, async. Body counting skips plain strings, raw strings (r"..", r#".."#), char literals such as '{' and `//` comments. A call is the name at an identifier boundary (previous char not alphanumeric, `_` or `.`), followed by `(` or `::<`, on a non-comment test-region line other than the fn line. Same-file wrappers always count. A pub or pub(crate) wrapper also counts for other files of the SAME crate (crate id = the path component after `crates/`, or `xtask`); fns under crates/athena-testkit/src/ are skipped. D163 states the limits: a wrapper that takes the mode as a parameter (no literal in its body) is not found; a name collision inside one crate is fixed by renaming or an EXEMPT entry.
decisions.reason: claude.rs:240-249 `write_private` sets `.mode(0o600)`, a private non-executable file; the round-2 rule would have flagged any test call to it. Requiring an execute bit makes the rule about stand-ins, not about any mode setter. Real wrappers all carry a 0o755 literal (toolconfig.rs:17, git/snapshot.rs:477, xtask set_executable). Same-crate matching stops a common pub name in one crate from flagging unrelated calls in another. Literal-aware counting stops a '{' char literal from running a body past its end.

decisions.choice: chmod-in-argument rule: a non-comment test-region line containing the word `chmod` plus one of `Command::new(`, `.arg(`, `.args(`, `"sh"`, `"bash"` or the quoted flag `"-c"`; or a line whose first token is `"chmod"` right after a line ending `Command::new(`. The old `Command::new(` + `chmod"` hit keeps its reason `chmod child`; new hits report `chmod argument`. Lines inside a write_executable( call are skipped. The span is found by a literal-aware scanner (plain, raw and char literals) starting at the `write_executable(` text and ending at the first line where paren depth returns to zero (answers finding 8). If depth has not returned to zero within 40 lines the span is only the opening line, so a runaway span cannot hide later violations.
decisions.reason: Real helper calls put the script on later lines (checks.rs:1003-1006, reconcile.rs:134-137), so a script line that mentions chmod must pass. Stand-in scripts are often raw strings (claude.rs STAND_IN const uses r#".."#) holding `$(` or `)`; counting parens inside them would stretch the span. The quoted `"-c"` avoids `git -c` and `--cached` strings. Policy inputs like `"chmod +x src/lib.rs"` (policy.rs:1201) have no marker.

rejected.option: Count parens outside ordinary strings only, capped at 40 lines
rejected.why: A raw-string `$(` keeps depth above zero and hides up to 40 following lines.

risks.risk: The wrapper rule flags a legitimate test call (a mode setter that is not a stand-in, or a shared name used by an unrelated fn).
risks.mitigation: A wrapper needs a raw permission call plus an execute-bit signal, so 0o600 and write-bit toggles pass; matching is by whole identifier and limited to the same crate; testkit/src is skipped. Fixtures pin 0o600, the write-bit toggle, the one-letter name, private-not-flagged and cross-crate-not-flagged. The real-tree test shows the result; a hit is fixed or given a documented EXEMPT entry, never silently loosened.

risks.risk: A wrapper escapes: it takes the mode as a parameter, or is called under another name from another crate.
risks.mitigation: D163 states these limits. The primitive scan still flags any direct permission call in test code, and the retry is a second layer.

risks.risk: The chmod rule misses a split form or flags a policy string or helper script body; a raw-string script stretches the helper span and hides violations.
risks.mitigation: The rule needs the word chmod plus a command-building marker, a quoted "-c", and skips write_executable( calls using a literal-aware span that ends at the first zero depth and fails closed past 40 lines. Fixtures cover a policy array, `git -c`, a multi-line helper call, a raw string with `$(`, and an unclosed call.

risks.risk: The retry masks a real fault or slows a failing run.
risks.mitigation: At most 20 attempts of 50 ms (about 1 s), only on ETXTBSY; the last error is returned unchanged; other errors return at once. Unit tests pin the bound and the pass-through.

risks.mitigation: A std Command keeps its settings after a failed spawn. The producer builds `let mut cmd` first and wraps only the final spawn/output/status call; the compiler and the existing tests check it.

demonstrations.method: Read the new fixture tests in the scan file.
demonstrations.observes: Flagged fixtures: a pub wrapper above #[cfg(test)] called from test code; a test-only wrapper and its call; a generic wrapper `fn mark<P: AsRef<Path>>`; a cross-file pub wrapper in the same crate via violations_with, and the same fn private not flagged, and a same-name pub fn in another crate not flagged; a one-letter wrapper `t` where only the real call is flagged; `sh -c` with a chmod string; .arg("chmod"); .args(["-c", "chmod +x t"]); split `Command::new(` then `"chmod"`; a multi-line write_executable with a raw string holding `$(` followed by a set_permissions line, which is flagged; an unclosed call fails closed. Not-flagged fixtures: single-line and multi-line write_executable calls whose script line mentions chmod; a write-bit toggle fn (`| 0o200`, `& !0o222`); a `.mode(0o600)` fn called from test code; a fn with a '{' char literal; a `git -c` shell string; a policy-style `["chmod +x src/lib.rs"]` array.

Without the chmod rule the shell-string, .arg, .args and split-Command fixtures fail. Without the literal-aware span the raw-string fixture's set_permissions line is skipped and not flagged. If the rules over-reached, the asserted-empty fixtures (helper, 0o600, write-bit, policy array) and the real-tree test fail.
